tur23-1: Painkillers: Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether you need one and which is right for you.
tur23-2: Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether you need a painkiller and which one is right for you; this is especially important if you have asthma, high blood pressure, or kidney, heart or stomach problems.
tur23-3: If you need a painkiller, ask your doctor or pharmacist which one to use and how; if your pain does not go away, seek advice again.
tur23-4: Ask your doctor or pharmacist before taking a painkiller for a headache; Ireland’s health service (HSE) recommends paracetamol rather than ibuprofen or aspirin during this period, as they could increase bleeding. You can put ice wrapped in a towel on any swelling.
tur23-5: HSE (Health Service Executive, Ireland). Head injury and concussion. Last reviewed 20 September 2024.
tur23-6: Exercises are easier when your pain is under control. If you are going to take a painkiller, ask your doctor or pharmacist which one to use and how; this is especially important if you have another condition or take other medicines.
tur23-7: Usually not. The advice is to move the neck gradually and carry on with your daily activities as far as possible. Exercises are easier when your pain is under control; if you are going to take a painkiller, ask your doctor or pharmacist.
tur23-8: Ask your child’s doctor or your pharmacist before giving a painkiller; the type of medicine and the dose depend on your child’s age and weight. Do not give aspirin to children under 16 unless a doctor recommends it.
tur23-9: Exercises are easier when your pain is under control; ask your doctor or pharmacist about painkillers.
tur23-10: Ask your doctor or pharmacist before taking a painkiller.
tur23-11: Painkillers act too slowly to help during a cramp; for any pain left afterwards, ask your doctor or pharmacist before taking medicine.
tur23-12: Heat or cold can bring relief; ask your doctor or pharmacist about a painkiller or painkilling gel.
tur23-13: If you have pain, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether to take a painkiller.
